content: Aerolíneas Argentinas Flight 670 was a domestic flight that crashed on October 12, 1996, near the city of San Carlos de Bariloche, in the Río Negro Province of Argentina. The aircraft was a Boeing 737-287 that was flying from Buenos Aires to Bariloche. During its approach to the airport, the plane crashed into a mountain, killing all 74 people on board. The cause of the accident was determined to be pilot error, with poor visibility and adverse weather conditions contributing to the crash. The investigation revealed that the pilots descended below the minimum safe altitude during the approach, leading to the fatal collision with the terrain.
